statement.p: Find the differential of f(x,y) = \sqrt{x^{3}+y^{2}} at the point (2,3).
Then use the differential to estimate f(2.1,2.9).

static.solution:
f_x(x,y) = and f_y(x,y) =, f_x(2,3) = and f_y(2,3) =.
Thus the differential at the point (2,3) is df = df(2,3) = f_x(2,3)\,dx + f_y(2,3)\,dy = 1.45521dx+0.727607dy.
Using the differential at the point (2,3), we can estimate f(2.1,2.9). Since \Delta f \approx f_x(2,3)\Delta x + f_y(2,3)\Delta y, where \Delta f = f(2.1,2.9) - f(2,3) and \Delta x = 2.1 - 2 and \Delta y = 2.9 - 3, we have f(2.1,2.9) \approx f(2,3) + f_x(2,3)(2.1-2) + f_y(2,3)(2.9-3) \approx 4.12311 + \,(0.1) + (-0.1) = 4.19587.
